title: BBVA places €1,000 million in a AT1 bond with demand seven times the issue size
summary: BBVA tapped the market on Tuesday with the issuance of a euro-denominated contingent convertible bond (‘CoCo’ or AT1) with a call option on October 18, 2034.
body_markdown:
BBVA placed €1,000 million in a contingent convertible bond (AT1) on Tuesday, with demand reaching as high as €8,250 million. The bond is perpetual but has a call window in October 2034. The coupon was set at 6.5%, significantly below the initial price guidance of 7.125%. The coupon is fixed, although if the bond is not redeemed on the specified date, it will become floating, linked to the five-year mid-swap rate plus a spread to be determined. The joint bookrunners were Barclays, BBVA, Bank of America, Citi, Deutsche Bank and Natixis.

This issuance brings forward part of the BBVA Group's 2027 funding plan and aims to strengthen its AT1 capital buffer.


This is the Group's eleventh debt issuance of the year. In January, the bank placed €2,000 million in a dual-tranche senior non-preferred (SNP) debt issuance, its largest euro-denominated issuance in the past 20 years. In February, BBVA placed $2,500 million in another senior non-preferred debt issuance, the largest in its history in this currency. In April, it placed $2,250 million in a dual-tranche issuance, comprising $1,250 million in SNP debt and $1,000 million in AT1 debt. In June, the bank placed €1,250 million in a senior non-preferred green bond issuance and €2,250 million in a dual-tranche covered bond issuance, its first since 2023. In August, it placed $2,300 million in a three-tranche issuance. In September, it placed a further €1,250 million in a senior preferred green bond and £600 million in a senior non-preferred bond. In November, the Group placed CHF 390 million in a dual-tranche senior preferred green bond issuance and $2,050 million in a three-tranche senior non-preferred bond issuance
